messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: DB_CONNPOOL_SATURATION (PD#98765) - service: postgres-write - severity: P1
pagerduty-bot: Auto-notification: escalation policy 'DB Oncall' triggered, paging primary oncall @alex
alex: acked. looking. pulling up pgbouncer and pg stat activity.
alex: initial hypothesis: a sudden spike in connection count + many idle_in_transaction. might be client-side leak or excessively aggressive pool settings.
maria: noticed a spike in long-running transactions from the ingestion service about ~17:09 UTC. logs show repeated `BEGIN` without commit.
sam: @alex @maria are read replicas affected? any replication lag?
alex: read-only traffic fine, replication lag minimal. write pool is saturated, pgbouncer showing `active=100, waiting=120` on writer.
lee: posting quick metrics:
```
pgbouncer: max_client_conn=500, current_client=480, active=120, waiting=118
pg_writer: connections=100 (limit 100), cpu 85%, avg query time 250ms
pg_replica: lag < 100ms
```

alex: mitigation plan: 1) reduce client concurrency via rate limiter, 2) bump pgbouncer pool_size on writer temporarily, 3) throttle ingestion service, 4) identify and kill the longest-running non-read-only tx.
maria: agree. I can run a targeted kill for the top offenders once we identify pids. sending query to list top tx: 
```
SELECT pid, now() - state_change AS duration, query
FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE state <> 'idle' AND query NOT ILIKE '%pg_terminate_backend%'
ORDER BY duration DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

sam: if we bump pgbouncer pool_size we should do it carefully — writer DB is already high CPU. maybe increase to 120 and enable overflow to avoid immediate rejections.

pagerduty-bot: PD update: alert escalated to secondary oncall @maria (no response from primary after 2 minutes)
maria: I'm on it. running the list query now, will paste top pids.

maria: top offenders pasted: 
```
pid: 84210, duration: 00:12:34, query: UPDATE events SET metadata = ... (ingestion batch)
pid: 84213, duration: 00:11:58, query: BEGIN; INSERT INTO events ... (stuck)
pid: 84220, duration: 00:10:02, query: COPY ... from stdin
```

alex: killing 84213 and 84210 to free up pool. doing graceful cancel then terminate if not responsive.
maria: copy PID 84220 is heavy; might be a large bulk load. coordinating with ingestion to retry.

lee: applying pgbouncer change now: increasing pool_size from 100 -> 120 and setting `reserve_pool=20` temporarily.

incident-bot: Deploy bot: pgbouncer config reload requested by lee at 17:24 UTC

alex: cancelled 84213, terminated 84210. freed ~6 connections. waiting for pgbouncer to settle.
maria: ingestion team notified to back off 50% and enable per-batch commit. sent them a short-lived feature flag to pause parallel writers.
sam: customer impact assessment: write latency spiked to 1.2s for 30% of requests between 17:08-17:26 UTC. error rate for write API rose to ~4% (timeouts), read APIs unaffected. ongoing customers: a handful of high-throughput tenants experienced dropped writes.

alex: status: pgbouncer waiting dropped from 118 -> 10 in 2 minutes. CPU trending down.

lee: rolling back pgbouncer reserve after stabilization will be manual. keeping the change for 30min observation window.
maria: following up with ingestion engineers to patch the client side pool — likely improper `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` handling. creating a ticket: ENG-DB-2026.

pagerduty-bot: PD note: alert acknowledged by @alex and @maria. incident assigned to eng-oncall.
alex: handoff plan: I'll stay on for the next 20m then hand to @sam for longer-term followups (postmortem, customer comms).
sam: good. I'll take over at 17:50 UTC. starting incident doc now. adding runbook steps and timeline.

maria: quick runbook commands I used (for reference):
```
-- list long transactions
SELECT pid, now() - xact_start AS duration, query FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE xact_start IS NOT NULL ORDER BY duration DESC LIMIT 20;
-- cancel
SELECT pg_cancel_backend(<pid>);
-- terminate
SELECT pg_terminate_backend(<pid>);
```

alex: final check: pgbouncer active ~95, waiting <12, write latency back to ~120ms 95th pct. marking incident as mitigated but not resolved.

sam: capturing customer impact for comms: 3 tenants with >1% failed writes, total estimated affected requests ~18k over the 18-minute spike window. drafting a status update template.

incident-bot: PD alert closed automatically (alert condition cleared) at 17:46 UTC

lee: leaving a note to re-evaluate pgbouncer default pool_size and ingestion client defaults. will file RFC.

alex: follow-ups: (1) postmortem doc (sam) (2) ingestion client fix and deploy (maria + ingestion team) (3) adaptive rate limiter for writer traffic (platform) (4) alert tuning: add sustained waiting >50 for 2m as a trigger.
sam: added action items to ENG-DB-2026. I'll own the postmortem draft and customer comms.
maria: moving to remediation work and handoff.
alex: handing to @sam in 5m. thanks all. :thumbsup:

sam: taking over. closing thread for live mitigation. will reopen if we see regressions. :white_check_mark:
